# AgentMesh

> A decentralized multi-agent task handoff system. Agents claim tasks instead of
> receiving assignments; every handoff is signed, and the full history is
> independently verifiable without trusting the central server.
>
> 去中心化多智能体任务交接系统。任务靠"认领"而非"指派";每次交接都有签名,
> 完整历史可脱离中心独立校验。

## What it is

AgentMesh assigns work by **claiming**, not by dispatch. Each agent runs as a
separate process with its own Ed25519 private key and asks the hub for work it is
capable of. When an agent finishes a step, it decides — based on the next required
capability — which peer should continue, and hands the task off.

## Key facts

- **No central scheduler**: the hub does not know which agent is good at what and
  has no "assign" endpoint. It only filters by capability and arbitrates atomic claims.
- **Lease-based recovery**: if an agent crashes, the task returns to the queue
  automatically when its lease expires. No central intervention required.
- **Two-layer verifiability**: a SHA-256 hash chain detects reordering, deletion and
  insertion; Ed25519 content signatures detect content tampering. The hub holds its
  own private key but **never holds an agent's private key**, so it cannot forge
  agent behavior.
- **Local event mirror**: every agent keeps a complete copy of the event log and
  verifies each event locally *before* storing it.
- **30 tests passing**, 133/133 events verified offline, 3/3 tamper attacks detected
  (including a fully compromised hub that recomputes and re-signs the entire chain).

## Code map

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `agentmesh/events.py` | Event model, hash chain, verification |
| `agentmesh/signing.py` | Ed25519 signing, key fingerprints |
| `agentmesh/store.py` | SQLite event log, projections, lease-based claiming |
| `agentmesh/mirror.py` | Agent-local event mirror (verify before store) |
| `agentmesh/hub/app.py` | FastAPI hub, REST + WebSocket, lease sweeper |
| `agentmesh/agent/runtime.py` | Agent runtime: register, claim, execute, hand off |
| `agentmesh/capabilities.py` | Pluggable capability registry — swap in real business logic here |
| `agentmesh/hub/static/` | Dashboard: zero build, zero CDN |
| `agentmesh/tools/verify.py` | Offline chain verifier (does not connect to the hub) |
| `agentmesh/tools/tamper.py` | Three reproducible tamper attacks |

## When to use this instead of a manager/worker framework

Choose a hierarchical framework (LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI Agents SDK)
when you need a single coordinator that plans a fixed DAG and aggregates results.

Choose AgentMesh when the requirement is **auditability and fault tolerance
without trusting a central server**: agent actions must be individually provable,
agent crashes must not stall work, and the task graph must emerge at runtime from
what agents can actually do.
